title: Bakery at Royal Crest: The science of a perfect cake
_note: say = text sent to ElevenLabs (numbers spelled out where they must be read a certain way); cap = on-screen caption. CHF uses 'Charlotte – Warm South African' from the account's voice list; swap voice_id for any voice in your account.

lines.say: Butter. Sugar. Eggs. Flour. Four plain ingredients.
lines.cap: Butter. Sugar. Eggs. Flour. Four plain ingredients.

lines.say: That's it? That's a cake?
lines.cap: That’s it? That’s a cake?

lines.say: Add a little science, and a lot of skill, and yes. That's a cake.
lines.cap: Add a little science, and a lot of skill, and yes. That’s a cake.

lines.say: Wait. Did you say science? In a kitchen?
lines.cap: Wait. Did you say science? In a kitchen?

lines.say: Welcome to the bakery at Royal Crest Academy, in Bikita. Today: the science of a perfect cake, from the mixing bowl to the business.
lines.cap: Welcome to the bakery at Royal Crest Academy, in Bikita. Today: the science of a perfect cake, from the mixing bowl to the business.

lines.say: Lesson one. The recipe. Two hundred and twenty-five grams each of butter, sugar and self-raising flour. Four eggs. A splash of milk.
lines.cap: Lesson one: the recipe. 225 g each of butter, sugar and self-raising flour. Four eggs. A splash of milk.

lines.say: Grams? Not cups?
lines.cap: Grams? Not cups?

lines.say: Grams. A baker weighs everything. Baking is chemistry, and chemistry needs exact amounts.
lines.cap: Grams. A baker weighs everything. Baking is chemistry, and chemistry needs exact amounts.

lines.say: Lesson two. Creaming. We beat the butter and sugar together until it turns pale and fluffy.
lines.cap: Lesson two: creaming. We beat the butter and sugar together until it turns pale and fluffy.

lines.say: Every sharp sugar crystal cuts tiny pockets into the butter, and traps millions of air bubbles.
lines.cap: Every sharp sugar crystal cuts tiny pockets into the butter, and traps millions of air bubbles.

lines.say: So the fluffy part is air?
lines.cap: So the fluffy part is air?

lines.say: Air. Then we beat in the eggs, one at a time, and fold in the flour gently, so we don't knock the air out.
lines.cap: Air. Then we beat in the eggs, one at a time, and fold in the flour gently, so we don’t knock the air out.

lines.say: Lesson three. Why a cake rises. Self-raising flour contains baking powder: bicarbonate of soda, and a dry acid.
lines.cap: Lesson three: why a cake rises. Self-raising flour contains baking powder: bicarbonate of soda, and a dry acid.

lines.say: Add liquid and heat, and they react, and release carbon dioxide gas.
lines.cap: Add liquid and heat, and they react, and release carbon dioxide gas.

lines.say: Wait. The same gas we breathe out?
lines.cap: Wait. The same gas we breathe out?

lines.say: The same gas. It flows into those air bubbles from the creaming, and blows them up like tiny balloons. The whole cake rises.
lines.cap: The same gas. It flows into those air bubbles from the creaming, and blows them up like tiny balloons. The whole cake rises.

lines.say: Lesson four. The oven, at one hundred and eighty degrees. Inside the tin, the cake changes in stages.
lines.cap: Lesson four: the oven, at 180 °C. Inside the tin, the cake changes in stages.

lines.say: First the gas expands and the batter rises. At about seventy degrees, the egg proteins set, and lock the bubbles in place.
lines.cap: First the gas expands and the batter rises. At about 70 °C, the egg proteins set, and lock the bubbles in place.

lines.say: Then the outside browns. Sugars and proteins react, and make that golden crust, and that smell.
lines.cap: Then the outside browns. Sugars and proteins react, and make that golden crust, and that smell.

lines.say: The best smell in the whole school.
lines.cap: The best smell in the whole school.

lines.say: Twenty-five minutes. Push a skewer into the middle. If it comes out clean, it's done.
lines.cap: 25 minutes. Push a skewer into the middle. If it comes out clean, it’s done.

lines.say: Lesson five. Building the cake. Two sponges, cooled completely.
lines.cap: Lesson five: building the cake. Two sponges, cooled completely.

lines.say: A layer of jam. A layer of buttercream. The second sponge. A thin crumb coat, then chill it, then the final coat.
lines.cap: A layer of jam. A layer of buttercream. The second sponge. A thin crumb coat, then chill it, then the final coat.

lines.say: Hold on. It's built in layers, like the house in the technical graphics film!
lines.cap: Hold on. It’s built in layers, like the house in the Technical Graphics film!

lines.say: Exactly. Plan it, build it in layers, and every layer has a job.
lines.cap: Exactly. Plan it, build it in layers, and every layer has a job.

lines.say: Lesson six. Icing. And there's more than one kind.
lines.cap: Lesson six: icing. And there’s more than one kind.

lines.say: Buttercream: soft butter and icing sugar, beaten until smooth. Perfect for piping.
lines.cap: Buttercream: soft butter and icing sugar, beaten until smooth. Perfect for piping.

lines.say: Royal icing: egg white and icing sugar. It sets hard, so it's used on wedding cakes.
lines.cap: Royal icing: egg white and icing sugar. It sets hard, so it’s used on wedding cakes.

lines.say: Fondant: a soft sugar paste. We roll it out like a sheet, and drape it over the cake.
lines.cap: Fondant: a soft sugar paste. We roll it out like a sheet, and drape it over the cake.

lines.say: And chocolate ganache: warm cream and melted chocolate, poured over the top so it drips.
lines.cap: And chocolate ganache: warm cream and melted chocolate, poured over the top so it drips.

lines.say: Wait. Is that our school crest, on the cake?
lines.cap: Wait. Is that our school crest, on the cake?

lines.say: It is. First a crumb coat, then chill it. Smooth the final coat with a palette knife on a turntable. Then pipe, with a bag and a star nozzle, and a steady hand.
lines.cap: It is. First a crumb coat, then chill it. Smooth the final coat with a palette knife on a turntable. Then pipe, with a bag and a star nozzle, and a steady hand.

lines.say: Lesson seven. Every cake is different. A Victoria sponge: light and simple, with jam and cream.
lines.cap: Lesson seven: every cake is different. A Victoria sponge: light and simple, with jam and cream.

lines.say: Chocolate cake, rich and dark. And red velvet: a soft red sponge, with cream cheese icing.
lines.cap: Chocolate cake, rich and dark. And red velvet: a soft red sponge, with cream cheese icing.

lines.say: Red velvet. Now that's my favourite.
lines.cap: Red velvet. Now that’s my favourite.

lines.say: Carrot cake, moist and spiced. Fruit cake, packed with raisins, cherries and peel, under marzipan and royal icing. It keeps for months, so it's the classic wedding cake.
lines.cap: Carrot cake, moist and spiced. Fruit cake, packed with raisins, cherries and peel, under marzipan and royal icing. It keeps for months, so it’s the classic wedding cake.

lines.say: And wine cake: a rich, dark fruit cake soaked in red wine, for weddings and big celebrations.
lines.cap: And wine cake: a rich, dark fruit cake soaked in red wine, for weddings and big celebrations.

lines.say: Birthdays, weddings, graduations. A cake is the centre of every celebration, and people pay well for a beautiful one.
lines.cap: Birthdays, weddings, graduations. A cake is the centre of every celebration, and people pay well for a beautiful one.

lines.say: Okay. So how much does a cake actually make?
lines.cap: Okay. So how much does a cake actually make?

lines.say: Lesson eight. Costing. Add up every ingredient, the electricity and the box. Say, nine dollars.
lines.cap: Lesson eight: costing. Add up every ingredient, the electricity and the box. Say, $9.

lines.say: Sell the decorated cake for twenty-five dollars, and that's sixteen dollars profit. Bake five cakes a week, and it's a business.
lines.cap: Sell the decorated cake for $25, and that’s $16 profit. Bake five cakes a week, and it’s a business.

lines.say: Maths, science, and money. In one cake.
lines.cap: Maths, science, and money. In one cake.

lines.say: So what does this mean for a child from Bikita?
lines.cap: So what does this mean for a child from Bikita?

lines.say: A skill for life. Baker. Pastry chef. Cake designer. Hotel and catering chef. Food technologist. Or the owner of their own bakery.
lines.cap: A skill for life. Baker. Pastry chef. Cake designer. Hotel and catering chef. Food technologist. Or the owner of their own bakery.

lines.say: And every wedding, every hotel and every supermarket in Zimbabwe needs bakers.
lines.cap: And every wedding, every hotel and every supermarket in Zimbabwe needs bakers.

lines.say: At Royal Crest, it starts in Form One. Bakery and Food Production is a practical trade, alongside the sciences, and taught for ZIMSEC, Cambridge and HEXCO.
lines.cap: At Royal Crest, it starts in Form 1. Bakery and Food Production is a practical trade, alongside the sciences, and taught for ZIMSEC, Cambridge and HEXCO.

lines.say: Science. Innovation. Skill. Your child leaves with a certificate, and a skill they can earn from.
lines.cap: Science. Innovation. Skill. Your child leaves with a certificate, and a skill they can earn from.

lines.say: Parents: Form One places for January twenty twenty-seven are limited.
lines.cap: Parents: Form 1 places for January 2027 are limited.

lines.say: Come and taste it for yourself.
lines.cap: Come and taste it for yourself.

lines.say: Bake it with science. Sell it with skill.
